title: Tôi quên đồ rồi
summary: Say "I left something behind" with Tôi quên đồ rồi, then use the notes below to adjust tone and next steps.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: For travelers, Tôi quên đồ rồi is the phrase to keep ready for "I left something behind" in lost items, help, managers, and recovery moments. Say this if you forgot an item in a car, room, or café. This is a common hotel, taxi, and café recovery phrase. It works best when you focus on saying what went missing before you add where or when it happened. After you say it, listen for a question about the last place, a room or ride check, or a staff handoff; the next rows help you keep the exchange moving.

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: Listen to each piece, then the whole phrase, so the rhythm feels connected instead of memorized word by word.

sections.title: The standard way
sections.body: Use Tôi quên đồ rồi as your first sentence for "I left something behind". Say this if you forgot an item in a car, room, or café. Leave a short pause after the phrase so the other person can answer with a question about the last place, a room or ride check, or a staff handoff. Keep a receipt, room number, ride detail, or last location visible when it helps staff trace the problem.

sections.title: Why it matters
sections.body: Help phrases work when they name the problem and the next person or action you need. For "I left something behind", Tôi quên đồ rồi helps by saying what went missing before you add where or when it happened. Have the receipt, room number, ride detail, or last location ready if they ask.

sections.title: Traveler insight
sections.body: In Problems & Help, the reply often comes as a question about the last place, a room or ride check, or a staff handoff. Say Tôi quên đồ rồi once, pause, and watch for the reply before adding another sentence. Keep a receipt, room number, ride detail, or last location visible when it helps staff trace the problem.
